causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: A planned network outage of the Tarong to Braemar line reduced available supplies in the region, constraining off generati on in south west Queensland and forcing flows across the interconnector into New South Wales counter pri ce.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding of capacity into higher prices by Stanwell, combined with an unplanned outage of CS Energy's Swanbank unit E, drove the price in Queensland to exceed $5000/MWh.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Rebidding of capacity into higher prices by Stanwell, combined with an unplanned outage of CS Energy's Swanbank unit E, drove the price in Queensland to exceed $5000/MWh.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: A planned outage of a Tarong to Braemar 275kV line between 5.25 am and 4.25 pm reduced the capability for flows into the Brisbane load centre from generation in south west Queensland (a total of around 2380 MW of ava ilable capacity) and from New South Wales across QNI (750 MW nominal capability).

constraints_named.quote: From 5.25 am, when the outage commenced, a c onstraint was invoked th at saw QNI forced to flow into New South Wales at more than 900 MW.

constraints_named.id: NEMMCO additional constraint for negative residue management
constraints_named.quote: At 5.45 am NEMMCO intervened with an additional constraint to reduce the counter price flows to 750 MW.

interconnectors_named.name: QNI
interconnectors_named.quote: A planned outage of a Tarong to Braemar 275kV line between 5.25 am and 4.25 pm reduced the capability for flows into the Brisbane load centre from generation in south west Queensland (a total of around 2380 MW of ava ilable capacity) and from New South Wales across QNI (750 MW nominal capability).

intervals.quote: On Sunday 4 November, the spot price in Queensland exceeded $5000/MWh in two trading intervals, reaching $5723/MWh at midda y and $6000/MWh at 12.30 pm.

network_outages.quote: A planned network outage of the Tarong to Braemar line reduced available supplies in the region, constraining off generati on in south west Queensland and forcing flows across the interconnector into New South Wales counter pri ce.

peak_price.quote: On Sunday 4 November, the spot price in Queensland exceeded $5000/MWh in two trading intervals, reaching $5723/MWh at midda y and $6000/MWh at 12.30 pm.

rebid_set_price.quote: The rebi dding, combined w ith an unplanned outage of CS Energy's Swanbank unit E, was th e primary driver of the high prices around midday. Spot prices would have been ar ound $100/MWh in the ab sence of Stanwell's rebidding.
